newsitem.title: USA: New York orders $109.6 mln NYNEX rebates.
newsitem.headline: New York orders $109.6 mln NYNEX rebates.

text.p: The New York Public Service Commission on Wednesday ordered NYNEX Corp to return a total $109.6 million to customers in the state.

The commission said $87 million is for improper dealings with affiliates between 1984 and 1991, and $22.6 million was for quality of service rebates. The quality rebates include $10 million from a denial of a waiver sought by NYNEX.
However, the commission said that NYNEX improved its performance on all 16 quality measures in the last quarter of 1996 compared with the year-earlier period.

The affiliates case began in 1990 when the commission said New York Telephone had been overcharged by another NYNEX unit, NYNEX Material Enterprises Co, for removing telephone switches and related equipment.
This and another case, over rates charged by NYNEX Information Resources to New York Telephone, went to court but by November 1996 had not been resolved.
Instead NYNEX and the commission have made an agreement which includes clauses to stop these type of affiliate transactions occurring, the commission said.

NYNEX will refund $53 million plus interest for the NYNEX Material Enterprises case, and $30 million plus interest for the NYNEX Information Resources case. This totals $87 million, to be credited on consumer bills within 90 days.
The quality of service rebates concern a regulatory plan which began in 1995 to replace rate of return regulation with a system of price controls and quality hurdles.

In November 1996 the commission said NYNEX's performance warranted $72.9 million of penalties. Of this $617,000 was waived and $10 million suspended pending a NYNEX claim of miscalaculation of performance data, the commission said.
The commission said that while there were some errors, the penalty was still warranted and ordered the $10 million to be refunded within 30 days.

The additional quality penalties are $9 million for weakspots in fault reporting and lines out of service for more than 24 hours, and $3.6 million because the commission ruled out extensions for improving customer inquiry handling.
NYNEX said that the commission had not yet decided how the rebates will be distributed, but it could average $9.70 per line for the 10 million lines the company has in New York.
"This is a day that NYNEX saw final closure of a number of long standing issues," spokesman Bob Varettoni said.
"While we did pay a high price to clear the decks, we are now moving forward to the exciting opportunities that await us," he said.
NYNEX said it had established reserves to cover all the rebates, and there would be no effect on earnings . (( Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712))
